description: Replace naive calendar-day addition with business-day addition that skips weekends and is exact for any starting weekday
prompts: dates.py's add_days(start, n) just does `start + timedelta(days=n)` - it counts weekends as business days, which is wrong for anything scheduling-related. Implement add_business_days(start: date, n: int) -> date: n=0 returns start unchanged (even if start itself falls on a weekend); for n>0, step forward day by day, skipping Saturdays and Sundays, until n business days have been counted, and return that date. It must be exact for any starting weekday and correctly cross month/year boundaries - do not use an approximation formula like `n + 2*(n//5)` calendar-days shortcut, it gives the wrong answer depending on which weekday `start` falls on.

test_setup_files.test_dates_hidden.py:
from datetime import date

from dates import add_business_days


def test_zero_returns_start_unchanged():
    d = date(2024, 6, 1)  # a Saturday
    assert add_business_days(d, 0) == d


def test_friday_plus_one_skips_weekend():
    friday = date(2024, 5, 31)
    assert add_business_days(friday, 1) == date(2024, 6, 3)  # Monday


def test_monday_plus_five_lands_next_monday():
    monday = date(2024, 5, 27)
    assert add_business_days(monday, 5) == date(2024, 6, 3)


def test_crosses_month_and_year_boundary():
    # Friday Dec 27 2024 + 3 business days: Mon 30, Tue 31, Wed Jan 1 2025
    friday = date(2024, 12, 27)
    assert add_business_days(friday, 3) == date(2025, 1, 1)


def test_starting_on_a_weekend_still_counts_correctly():
    saturday = date(2024, 6, 1)
    assert add_business_days(saturday, 1) == date(2024, 6, 3)  # Monday
